$comment: What each column of each Martinec et al. (2018) data file holds, decoded from the GMT 4 scripts that drew the published figures. Generated by scripts/decode_gmt_layouts.py; do not edit by hand. Paths are relative to data/original/. For files with no header these scripts are the only surviving record, and GMT 4 no longer runs. `negated` means the script plots the negative of the column, which is how several contributors' geoid sign is reconciled. `scale` records arithmetic applied before plotting, with the column written as x. The last three sections are transcribed from file headers or established by arithmetic, and carry their evidence.

vega_seven_column_format.$comment: The seven-column format VEGA writes for a cross-section, taken verbatim from the header of martinec2018/resultsA_2026/Z_ZM_load.out, which is the only file that carries one. The same format is used by every Z_ZM_{load,basin}.out and by the Z_*_diff.out files of cases B, C and D, where column n is the contributor minus VEGA. The case A difference files and the two WW files of case B hold four or five columns, which are a subset in the same order.

columns.name: abscissa
columns.description: Longitude in a figY_uvf cross-section, colatitude in a figZ_uvf one

columns.name: V_phi
columns.description: Longitude component of horizontal displacement. NaN at colatitude 0 and 180, where it is undefined.

columns.name: potential
columns.description: Gravitational potential increment. Divide by the surface gravity 9.8155 to obtain geoid height N, which is what the plotting scripts do. In a difference file this column is already a geoid height difference in metres.

columns.name: S
columns.description: Sea-surface variation with respect to the uniform water layer h_UF

vega_time_series_format.$comment: The eleven-column time series VEGA writes for cases C, D and E. The header is transcribed from martinec2018/resultsC_2026/vega76.out. secti.out has no header and the same layout except column 5; see correction martinec2018-secti-column5.

columns.name: ocean_area
columns.note: The header says per cent. The values are a fraction: 0.04628693 at t = 0, which every script multiplies by 100.

columns.header: huf4=mass of water displayed by ice/ofj00
